metadata.description: Evidence-based exercise library for sports injury rehabilitation. Based on PubMed and Consensus research.

exercises.description: Supine position. Slowly raise the injured leg with knee extended until gentle stretch felt. Hold 30 seconds. Avoid pain. Knee may be slightly bent in acute phase.
exercises.progression_criteria: Pain-free stretch to 70° hip flexion before progressing to dynamic stretching

exercises.description: Standing, place heel on surface at hip height with knee extended. Hinge forward at hips maintaining neutral spine. Hold 30 seconds.
exercises.progression_criteria: Achieve comfortable stretch before adding dynamic movements
contraindications: acute grade 2-3 tear in first 72 hours

exercises.description: Prone lying. Slowly curl heel toward buttock through pain-free range. Emphasize slow controlled eccentric lowering phase (3-4 seconds down).
exercises.progression_criteria: 3 sets of 15 pain-free before adding resistance

exercises.description: Stand with feet hip-width. Hinge at hips, pushing them back while lowering barbell/dumbbells along shins. Knee slightly bent. Maintain neutral spine. Focus on hip extension pattern to activate biceps femoris long head.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress weight when 3x12 achieved with good form and <2/10 pain

exercises.description: Kneel with feet anchored. Arms crossed over chest. Slowly lower body forward under control using hamstrings (eccentric phase 3-4 seconds). Catch with hands, push back up. Begin with 2-3 reps per set with full assistance, progressively reduce assistance.
exercises.progression_criteria: Work toward 3x10 without hand assistance. Key for fascicle length adaptation and injury prevention.

exercises.description: Position on a 45° back extension apparatus. Start with hips at top, hinge forward to ~45° then drive hips into extension. Focus on hamstring and glute drive. Emphasizes biceps femoris long head activation over Nordic curl.
exercises.progression_criteria: 3x12 with bodyweight, then add external load

exercises.description: Stage-based running: (1) walking, (2) jogging 50% speed, (3) striding 70%, (4) 85% sprinting with change of direction. Each stage pain-free before progressing. Sprinting criteria: pain-free sprinting required before return to sport.
exercises.progression_criteria: Pain-free at each speed level AND sprint mechanics assessment. Expert consensus: pain-free criteria specifically required for sprinting (85.5% agreement in international Delphi).

exercises.description: Seated or lying with leg straight. Contract quadriceps pushing back of knee into surface. Hold 5-10 seconds. Used in immediate post-op/acute phase to maintain quad activation without joint loading.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress when pain and swelling permit range of motion exercises

exercises.description: Feet shoulder-width. Squat to 30-60° knee flexion only. Weight through heels. Maintain knee alignment over 2nd toe. Closed kinetic chain reduces ACL graft strain compared to open chain exercises in early phase.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress range to full squat as pain and ROM allow; progress to single-leg

exercises.description: Bilateral leg press machine. Start with high foot position on plate (hip-dominant). Progress to lower foot position increasing quadriceps demand. Progress from both legs to single leg. Load target: 70-85% 1RM for strength phase.
exercises.progression_criteria: Single-leg leg press ≥85% of contralateral limb before plyometric introduction
contraindications: acute graft healing phase (weeks 0-6 post ACLR)

exercises.description: Stand on one leg, squat to 60-90° while maintaining knee alignment over toes. Arms forward for balance. Assess quality: knee should not cave inward. Progression: add load, increase depth, speed.
exercises.progression_criteria: Consistent good form with knee tracking, symmetric limb symmetry index ≥90%

exercises.description: Jump onto box (30-60cm) landing softly with knees bent and hips back. Focus on quiet, controlled landing. Progress from bilateral to unilateral. Criteria-based introduction: quad strength ≥70% LSI, no effusion.
exercises.progression_criteria: Bilateral box jump with good form before progressing to unilateral
contraindications: limb symmetry index <70% on strength testing

exercises.description: Hop forward as far as possible on one leg, land and stick the landing. Measure distance. Used as return-to-sport test: target ≥90% limb symmetry index compared to contralateral leg. Also assesses dynamic stability.
exercises.progression_criteria: ≥90% LSI, symmetric landing mechanics, confidence rating ≥7/10

exercises.description: Resistance band around ankles/knees. Semi-squat position. Step laterally maintaining hip-width gap. Keep toes forward, no trunk sway. Strengthens hip abductors and external rotators, critical for knee valgus control.
exercises.progression_criteria: Increase band resistance, progress to standing lateral band walk
contraindications: acute medial knee pain exacerbated by hip ER

exercises.description: Seated with foot elevated. Draw letters A-Z with big toe, moving only ankle. Perform in all planes: dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, inversion, eversion. Maintains range of motion and reduces swelling.
exercises.progression_criteria: Full pain-free ROM in all planes before weight-bearing exercises

exercises.description: Stand with feet hip-width. Rise onto toes slowly (2 sec up, 2 sec down). Progress to edge of step for increased range. Targets gastrocnemius and soleus. Progress to single leg.
exercises.progression_criteria: 30 pain-free bilateral reps before progressing to single-leg

exercises.description: Stand on injured leg for 30-60 seconds. Eyes open first, then eyes closed. Progress to unstable surface (foam pad, balance board). Restores proprioception impaired after ankle sprain.
exercises.progression_criteria: 60 seconds stable on firm surface with eyes closed before moving to unstable

exercises.exercise_name: Star Excursion Balance Test / Y-Balance Training
exercises.description: Stand on one leg. Reach opposite foot in anterior, posteromedial, and posterolateral directions as far as possible while maintaining balance. Return to start between reaches. Measures and trains dynamic balance.
exercises.progression_criteria: Symmetric reach distances (≥90% compared to uninjured) before return-to-sport

exercises.description: Hop laterally side-to-side over a line or low hurdle on one or two feet. Begin with two feet, progress to single-leg lateral hops. Key test for ankle functional clearance.
exercises.progression_criteria: 10 consecutive single-leg lateral hops with good control and <2/10 pain

exercises.description: Set up 4 cones in T-shape. Sprint forward, shuffle laterally, backpedal. Measures multi-directional agility. Used as return-to-sport functional test along with single-leg hop tests.
exercises.progression_criteria: Symmetric agility times and confidence rating before unrestricted play

exercises.description: Lean forward, let arm hang freely. Use trunk momentum to swing arm in small circles and side-to-side. Gravity-assisted distraction reduces pain and maintains range of motion without rotator cuff activation.
exercises.progression_criteria: Comfortable pendulum motion before adding active-assisted ROM exercises
contraindications: acute rotator cuff rupture requiring surgical repair

exercises.description: Elbow at side, bent 90°. Theraband attached to fixed point. Rotate arm outward away from body. Targets infraspinatus and teres minor. 2-second hold at end range. Start with light resistance.
exercises.progression_criteria: 3x15 with good control, progress band resistance every 2 weeks

exercises.description: Elbow at side, bent 90°. Rotate arm inward across body against band resistance. Targets subscapularis. Balance with external rotation work. Often IR is overworked; use ratio of ER:IR = 1:1 to 2:1.
exercises.progression_criteria: Match progression of external rotation exercise
contraindications: anterior instability exacerbated by IR loading

exercises.exercise_name: Scapular Retraction / Prone T's, Y's, W's
exercises.description: Prone on bench or floor. Lift arms into T (90° abduction), Y (120°), and W (90° ER) positions. Squeeze shoulder blades together. Targets lower and middle trapezius, rhomboids. Critical for scapular stabilization.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress to light dumbbells (1-3 kg), then increase as tolerated
contraindications: acute pain exacerbated by prone positioning

exercises.description: Seated dumbbell press. Begin at 90° of abduction, progress to full overhead. Requires pain-free active ROM first. Low weight, high control initially. Sport-specific: overhead athletes require full overhead strength.
exercises.progression_criteria: Full pain-free ROM with load before sport-specific throwing progression

exercises.description: Seated with knee bent at 60°. Push leg against immovable surface (wall or leg press). Hold contraction for 45 seconds at 70% maximum voluntary contraction. Immediate analgesic effect on tendon pain, cortical inhibition reduction.
exercises.progression_criteria: When pain reduces to <3/10 with isometrics, begin isotonic loading

exercises.description: Stand on 25° decline board on one leg. Slowly lower to 60° knee flexion (4-second eccentric), pause 2 seconds, rise (4-second concentric). Progress load using weighted vest or barbell. Target 70-90% 1RM. HSR is the reference standard for patellar tendinopathy.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress load weekly. VISA-P score improvement. Return to full sport when VISA-P ≥80.
contraindications: pain > 5/10 during or after exercise (NEXT-DAY pain monitoring)

exercises.description: Use flywheel device (YoYo, Exentric) or eccentric step machine to overload eccentric phase of knee extension. Provides supramaximal eccentric loads shown favorable in network meta-analysis (SMD 0.33 vs. HSR). Alternative to decline squat when equipment available.
exercises.progression_criteria: Pain monitoring: acceptable pain ≤4/10 during exercise, return to baseline within 24h

exercises.description: Progressive jumps: two-foot jumps → squat jumps → depth drops → single-leg bounds. Each stage pain-monitored. Required for return to jumping sports (volleyball, basketball). Only introduce when VISA-P ≥70 and HSR well-tolerated.
exercises.progression_criteria: VISA-P ≥80, pain-free jumping at each level before progressing

exercises.exercise_name: Alfredson Eccentric Heel Drop - Straight Knee
exercises.description: Stand on edge of step on injured foot, knee straight. Rise using both feet (concentric), lower slowly on injured foot only over 3 seconds (eccentric). Perform into pain - pain allowed up to 5/10. Protocol: 3x15 twice daily for 12 weeks. Targets gastrocnemius.
exercises.progression_criteria: Add load (backpack with weight) when 3x15 painless. Progress weekly.

exercises.exercise_name: Alfredson Eccentric Heel Drop - Bent Knee
exercises.description: Same as ACH_001 but with knee bent 45°. Isolates soleus muscle component. Perform in addition to straight-knee protocol. 3x15 twice daily. Both variants performed together = Alfredson's original 180 reps/day protocol.
exercises.progression_criteria: Completion of full 12-week protocol, return to sport when VISA-A ≥80

exercises.description: Stand on one foot on flat surface. Rise to tip-toe and hold at top position for 45 seconds at high effort (~70% MVC). Alternative to Alfredson in reactive phase. Analgesic and tendon-protective while avoiding heavy eccentric loads.
exercises.progression_criteria: Transition to isotonic loading when pain settles to <3/10

exercises.description: Seated calf raise machine or leg press. Load to ~90% of maximum voluntary contraction. Slow tempo: 3 seconds concentric, 3 seconds eccentric. Research shows superior tendon mechanical and morphological adaptations vs Alfredson protocol at this load.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress load weekly as tolerated. VISA-A improvement target ≥20 points.

exercises.description: Seated, cross injured foot over knee. Grasp toes and pull backward (dorsiflexion). Hold 10 seconds. Perform 10 repetitions before first step in morning and before standing after long rest. Direct tensioning of plantar fascia, superior to calf stretch alone.
exercises.progression_criteria: Consistent reduction in morning first-step pain

exercises.description: Stand facing wall. Place hands on wall. Step injured foot back, keep knee straight, heel on floor. Lean forward until calf stretch felt. Hold 30 seconds. Gastrocnemius tightness found in 80% of plantar fasciitis patients.
exercises.progression_criteria: Ankle dorsiflexion >10° before full weight-bearing exercises

exercises.exercise_name: Short Foot Exercise / Intrinsic Foot Strengthening
exercises.description: Seated then standing. Attempt to shorten the foot by drawing the ball of the foot toward the heel without curling toes. Activates intrinsic foot muscles (abductor hallucis). Hold 5-10 seconds. Progress to single-leg stance.
exercises.progression_criteria: Consistent activation without toe clawing, progress to standing on unstable surface
contraindications: severe foot pain preventing any foot muscle use

exercises.description: Stand on edge of step. Rise on toes, hold 2 seconds, slowly lower. This loads the plantar fascia through the windlass mechanism. Progress from bilateral to single-leg. Part of multimodal rehabilitation protocol.
exercises.progression_criteria: 20 pain-free bilateral reps before single-leg

exercises.description: Stand with injured leg crossed behind. Lean toward uninjured side while pushing hip of injured leg out. Feel stretch along outer thigh. Hold 30 seconds. Can perform against wall for support.
exercises.progression_criteria: Reduced lateral knee pain with movement before progressive loading

exercises.description: Side-lying with legs stacked. Lift top leg 30-45° and slowly lower. Leg straight, toes pointing slightly down. Targets gluteus medius, weakness of which is associated with IT band syndrome. Progress: ankle weight, resistance band.
exercises.progression_criteria: 3x20 with ankle weight before adding band resistance

exercises.description: Side-lying, hips stacked at 45°, knees at 90°. Rotate top knee upward like a clamshell while keeping feet together. Targets gluteus medius and external rotators. Use resistance band around thighs for progression.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress to weight-bearing hip external rotation exercises
contraindications: hip labral tear with ER-provoked pain

exercises.description: Supine with hips and knees bent to 45°. Place ball or foam pad between knees. Squeeze isometrically, hold 5-10 seconds. Begin with low force, increase as pain allows. Immediate pain-modulation effect.
exercises.progression_criteria: Pain-free isometric at hip in 45° flexion, 0° flexion before dynamic exercises

exercises.description: Side-lying, top foot on raised surface (bench/box). Lift hips off ground supporting weight on top leg (adductor contraction) and bottom forearm. Lower hips and lift again. Progressive variations: short lever (knee on bench) to long lever (foot on bench).
exercises.progression_criteria: Pain-free long-lever Copenhagen before return to kicking/pivoting sports

exercises.description: Comprehensive adductor strengthening program including: adductor/abductor isometrics, one-leg squat, reverse trunk curl, skating movements, ball squeezes. RCT demonstrated 79% return to sport at same level without groin pain. Long-lasting effect confirmed at 8-12 year follow-up.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress through protocol stages based on pain and strength; full return when pain-free with sport-specific loads

exercises.description: Supine with knees bent. Flatten lower back against floor by tightening abdominals (posterior tilt) then gently arch (anterior tilt). Gentle movement maintains mobility and reduces muscle spasm in acute phase.
exercises.progression_criteria: Reduction in acute spasm before progressing to core activation exercises

exercises.description: Four-point kneeling. Extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously while maintaining neutral spine (no rotation or hip drop). Hold 5-10 seconds. Core stabilization exercise from McGill protocol. Activates multifidus and contralateral erector spinae.
exercises.progression_criteria: 3x12 controlled before progressing to standing anti-rotation exercises
contraindications: acute disc herniation with radiculopathy exacerbated by extension

exercises.description: Supine. Arms straight up, hips and knees at 90°. Slowly lower opposite arm and leg toward floor while maintaining neutral lumbar spine (exhale and hollow abdomen). Return and alternate. Anti-extension core stability.
exercises.progression_criteria: 12 controlled reps per side before progressing to loaded exercises
contraindications: acute lumbar pain > 6/10 with trunk movement

exercises.exercise_name: McGill Big Three: Side Bridge / Side Plank
exercises.description: Side-lying on forearm with feet stacked. Lift hips forming straight line. Hold position. Progress from knees bent to full plank. One of McGill's 'Big Three' spine stabilization exercises. Targets lateral core and quadratus lumborum.
exercises.progression_criteria: 3x30 second holds before progressing to dynamic side plank variations
contraindications: lateral trunk pain exacerbated by this position

exercises.description: Progressive hip hinge pattern. Start with bodyweight, add load progressively. Focus on maintaining neutral spine, engaging lumbopelvic control. Key functional movement for athletes, replicates sporting demands on posterior chain.
exercises.progression_criteria: Pain-free with significant load before sport-specific return

exercises.description: Prone lying. Bend injured knee, reaching heel toward buttock. Can use towel or strap to assist. Hold 30 seconds. Avoid pain. In acute phase, perform in pain-free range only.
exercises.progression_criteria: Full ROM prone (heel to buttock) before progressing to resisted exercises

exercises.description: Back against wall, slide down to 45° knee flexion. Hold 10-30 seconds. Progress depth as tolerated. Gentle, controlled quad loading without full range of motion required.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress hold duration and depth before moving to full squat

exercises.description: Stand on step 10-20cm high. Slowly lower uninjured foot toward floor by bending injured knee. Control descent over 3-4 seconds. Tests quad strength and control during functional movement.
exercises.progression_criteria: Symmetric quality vs uninjured leg, add weight/height for progression
contraindications: significant knee valgus collapse during movement

exercises.description: Stand facing wall, hands on wall. Injured leg back with heel flat. Lean into wall feeling calf stretch. NO pain allowed in strain recovery. Begin when acute phase pain-free at rest.
exercises.progression_criteria: Full stretch without pain before resisted calf exercises
contraindications: acute grade 2-3 calf tear in first 48-72 hours

exercises.exercise_name: Calf Raise Progression (Bilateral to Single Leg)
exercises.description: Begin bilateral standing calf raises on flat ground. Progress to step edge. Then single-leg. Finally single-leg with load. Eccentric lowering emphasized (3-5 seconds). Watch for compensatory substitution.
exercises.progression_criteria: Symmetric strength to uninjured side: single-leg calf raise test (target 30+ reps)
contraindications: acute calf tear with active bleeding phase

exercises.description: Graded return: walking → slow jogging → moderate jogging → running → fast running. Each phase requires pain-free completion before advancement. Do not rush return to running; recurrence risk is high if progressed too quickly.
exercises.progression_criteria: Pain-free at current speed for 3 consecutive sessions before increasing

exercises.description: Kneeling on injured knee, front foot forward. Gently push hips forward until stretch felt at front of hip. Keep trunk upright. Hold 30 seconds. Avoid end-range in acute phase.
exercises.progression_criteria: Full hip extension ROM before adding strengthening exercises

exercises.exercise_name: Hip Flexor Strengthening (Standing Hip Flexion with Band)
exercises.description: Stand with resistance band around ankle. Lift knee to hip height against band resistance. Slow eccentric lowering. Targets iliopsoas in functional position. Begin with minimal resistance.
exercises.progression_criteria: Progress band resistance, then add weighted straight-leg raise
contraindications: pain > 4/10 during hip flexion against resistance

exercises.description: Forward lunge: step forward, lower back knee toward floor. Lateral lunge: step sideways, push hips back. Both load hip flexors and adductors in functional range. Key transition exercise before return to sport.
exercises.progression_criteria: Symmetric lunge mechanics before sport-specific acceleration/deceleration

exercises.description: Seated on edge of table. Actively flex and extend knee through available pain-free range. Gravity-assisted. Begin as soon as swelling allows. Prevents contracture and maintains joint nutrition.
exercises.progression_criteria: Full pain-free ROM before weight-bearing exercises

exercises.description: Stand with light resistance band behind knee. Push knee to full extension against band. Isolates VMO (medial quad) while avoiding valgus stress. Key early rehab for knee stability restoration.
exercises.progression_criteria: Pain-free with good VMO palpation before squatting exercises

exercises.description: Bodyweight squat focusing on valgus control. Use mirror/video feedback. Ensure knee tracks over 2nd toe without medial collapse. Progress from double to single-leg squat assessing MCL stability under functional load.
exercises.progression_criteria: Consistently good knee tracking before sport-specific lateral movements
contraindications: ongoing MCL instability with medial gapping

exercises.description: Walking in chest- or waist-deep water. Water buoyancy reduces weight-bearing by 60-80%. Allows early mobilization when land-based exercises are too painful. Progress from walking to jogging in pool.
exercises.progression_criteria: Transition to land-based exercises when acute pain resolves and full weight-bearing is possible

exercises.description: Supine, knees bent, feet flat. Drive hips upward into full extension squeezing glutes. Hold 2 seconds at top. Lower slowly. Progress: single-leg bridge, add resistance, elevate feet on bench.
exercises.progression_criteria: 3x20 pain-free before single-leg variant
contraindications: acute lumbar pain with hip extension

exercises.description: Bilateral jump: dip into quarter squat and explode upward. Measure height and symmetry. Used as both training and return-to-sport assessment tool. Asymmetry in CMJ linked to re-injury risk after ACLR. Target LSI ≥90%.
exercises.progression_criteria: CMJ LSI ≥90% is part of return-to-sport battery

exercises.description: Apply BFR cuff to upper limb of affected limb at 40-80% arterial occlusion pressure. Perform low-load exercises (20-30% 1RM) for high reps (30-15-15-15 protocol). Generates muscle hypertrophy and strength at loads tolerable in early post-injury/post-op phase.
exercises.progression_criteria: Transition to conventional loading when pain and tissue tolerance permit

exercises.description: Progressive footwork patterns through agility ladder: in-in-out-out, lateral shuffle, icky shuffle, Ali shuffle. Develops coordination, foot speed, and multi-directional movement required for sport. Begin slow, accelerate progressively.
exercises.progression_criteria: Completed at near-sport speed without compensation before unrestricted training
contraindications: ongoing pain with change of direction

exercises.description: Apply body weight through foam roller along muscle bellies of affected area. Apply pressure on tender spots for 30-60 seconds. Avoid rolling directly over injury site in acute phase. Precedes stretching or exercise.
exercises.progression_criteria: Adjunct modality; progress alongside primary exercises

exercises.description: Structured running progression based on RPE (6-20 scale or 0-10). Begin at RPE 3-4, increase duration first, then intensity. Monitor pain during and 24h post. Criterion-based progression: pain must return to baseline within 24h.
exercises.progression_criteria: Pain-free at current intensity for 3 sessions before increasing RPE target
contraindications: pain >3/10 during activity or persisting >24h after session

exercises.description: Sport-specific patterns: cutting maneuvers, deceleration, pivot stops, landing from jumps with correct mechanics. Performed with real-time feedback on technique. Critical final phase before return to unrestricted competition.
exercises.progression_criteria: Symmetric mechanics at game speed, psychological readiness assessed, >12 months post-ACLR
contraindications: limb symmetry index <90% on functional tests
